knowledge_answers.rationale: A called No ball does not count as one of the over.
The Wide penalty is added to the four-run boundary allowance; every resulting run is a Wide and is debited to the bowler.
The ball becoming dead does not itself end the appeal window; the appeal is timely before the next delivery's run-up begins or the innings closes.
The relevant state is frozen at the instant of the throw; two completed runs plus the crossed run in progress count; adding the four-run boundary allowance yields six.
LBW requires a delivery that is not a No ball; the geometric and interception conditions may all be satisfied; failure of the delivery-validity gate alone prevents LBW.
